messages.subject: Simulation of Intrinsic CAR process
parts:
Hi there


I am interested in simulating an intrinsic CAR process over a specific lattice (map). 
Does the INLA package can help on this? otherwise any advice (reference) on how to do this efficiently.
Without going into details, at the moment I am simulating from a Gaussian  random field
, a la geostatistics, and estimating using ICAR relying on the link between GRFs and GMRFs.

Karim

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simulation of Intrinsic CAR process
parts:
Hi Karim,
The problem with simulating an intrinisic CAR model is that it is
intrinsic and, therefore, improper. Therefore, it only makes sense to
simulate conditional on some constraints (such as a sum to zero
constraint).

So, I guess the first and most important question is: are you sure
you really want to do this! Have you considered using a proper model?
(also note - that the limiting GRF is also improper, being a Matern
field with kappa=0, and simulating from it is also non-trivial!)


The theoretical way of doing this is to compute the eigendecomposition
of the precision matrix (i.e. compute eigenpairs (lambda_i, e_i) ),
and do the following

Set x=0
For every non-zero lambda_i
Simulate y ~ N(0, lambda_i^{-1})
x = x + y*e_i
End For

If you are on a regular grid, you can use a FFT to compute the
eigendecomposition (see Håvard's book on GMRFs).

Of course, you often don't have an eigendecomposition! Another option,
if R [or matlab] will let you compute a Cholesky factorisation of an
positive semi-definite matrix, is compute the Cholesky decomposition Q
= L L^T, then the least-squares solution to L^Tx=z, where z is a
vector of i.i.d. standard normals will be a sample.

Another option is to let F be a matrix with columns that make a basis
for the nullspace of Q (i.e. QF =0). Then, sample from the proper
GMRF with precision Q + FF^T conditionally on F^Tx = 0.

If you want to go completely crazy, it's fairly straightforward to do
with Krylov Subspace methods, however, I probably wouldn't recommend
this route! It's a bit fiddly and, I suspect, more "expert
level"/"experimental" than you're looking for.

It possible that Håvard has a clever method that I haven't thought of,
but when it comes down to it, this is a slightly odd problem that I
don't think there is an elegant, efficient numerical solution to the
problem.

Hope this helps,
Dan

The limiting process of the ICAR when its parameter (conditional variance) tends to zero is a

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simulation of Intrinsic CAR process
parts:
Hi Karim,
This is a tricky question. In the end it depends on how the variance
parameter goes to zero. If the model is on a regular lattice and the
space between points is h, then, if the variance goes to zero like
h^2, then this limits towards a de Wijs field. If it goes to zero
faster than that, then it will shrink to zero (or, more specifically,
it will shrink to a de Wijs field with zero variance, which is an odd
thing). If it goes to zero slower, it will not converge to a limit.

Other than slightly insane "counter examples", I can't think of a GMRF
that limits to an i.i.d. process (i.e. white noise) that isn't the
same as having independent Gaussians on each component. In fact, I'm
pretty sure that "eventually", all GMRFs that limit to white noise
have to have this form.

Similarly, I'm struggling to come up with something that limits to a constant.

I hope this helps

Dan
